$comment: Descriptive, derived from the types the bounded parser reads; the parser is the only authority on validity. Where the parser reads two versions of a document with one type, this schema admits what that type admits, including members the later version adds. Byte, depth and count bounds are recorded in x-rustev-parse-limits (a string length here counts characters, the parser counts bytes), and rules applied when a plan is compiled are stated in field descriptions, not enforced here.

Attribution.description: How an exchange's charge reached its members (spec 009, 3.10.4).

oneOf.description: One member carries the whole charge.

Integer shares in attempt-id order over the members that received
the response; members that stopped waiting report `unknown`.

Charge.description: What an attempt cost, as far as is known when it ends.

Disclosure.description: What a served identity is worth (spec 009, 3.7).

oneOf.description: The remote side guarantees the identity.
The remote side said so; unverified.
Nothing is known. Never replaced by a requested model or a slug.

charge.description:
The charge supplied to the runtime for this member, or, in a late
record, the share offered for reconciliation.

oneOf.description: An output; `digest` is `sha256:` of its record canonical bytes.

PhaseExpiry.description:
The phase that ran out (spec 020, 3.4): its configured ceiling, the
effective allowance it started with (the lesser of the ceiling and the
remaining attempt budget), the time observed in it, whether request
bytes had left, and the existing code the expiry mapped to.

PhaseLimit.description:
What bounded a phase that ran out: its own ceiling, or the remaining
attempt budget when that was smaller (spec 020, 3.4).

PrincipalEvidence.description:
A principal reference as evidence holds it (spec 020, 3.2 and 3.6): its
domain-separated digest and mapping version, never the reference.

RemoteCode.description:
The closed error taxonomy (spec 009, 3.6). Each code maps to exactly one
spec 003 failure class; the mapping lives with the adapters, because the
failure classes of the backend seam are not contract types.

amount.description: A decimal string exactly as reported.

TransportPhase.description:
A transport phase with its own ceiling inside the one attempt budget
(spec 020, 3.4), in the order an exchange passes through them.

description:
One exchange, keyed by the attempt ids it served (spec 009, 3.9.1).
Bounded: every string is cut to [`MAX_TEXT_BYTES`] and every collection
to its cap by [`ExchangeRecord::bounded`], so a record never exceeds
[`EXCHANGE_V1`]'s `max_bytes`. Request and response bytes are never in
the record; only their digests are.

binding.description: The adapter binding identity (the adapter's artifact, 3.2.3).

bytes_sent.description: Whether any request byte left the process.

exchange_charge.description: The exchange's charge in deployment units, before attribution.

late.description:
The response arrived after the attempts stopped waiting; nothing in
it was supplied (3.4.4).

members.description: Every member attempt, in attempt-id order.

phase_expiry.description:
The transport phase that ran out, when an enabled phase policy
governed the exchange (spec 020, 3.4). Absent otherwise, so a record
without one keeps its spec 009 bytes.

principal.description:
The digest and mapping version of the principal reference the
request carried (spec 020, 3.6); absent when none was sent.

protocol.description: The wire protocol: [`PROTOCOL`] or a foreign mapping's own label.

reported_cost.description: Cost as reported, verbatim; units are not money.

request_digest.description: `sha256:` digest of the request bytes, when any were built.

response_digest.description: `sha256:` digest of the response bytes, when any were read.

truncated.description: Something was cut to fit the record's bounds.

usage.description: Usage as reported (for example token counts), by name.
